title: He Turns Abandoned Driving Ranges Into Cash Machines
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The guest discusses their own business and closes by naming its website and social channels, so there is promotional self-interest.

stated_problem.quote: Um, traditionally driving ranges very unwelcoming, stale experience. Uh, a lot of golfers complain about, hey, the turf quality isn't great.
stated_problem.speaker: Guest (name not stated)

idea.name: Acquire and modernize driving ranges
idea.one_liner: Buy dated driving ranges, improve the golfer experience, and earn from visits, memberships, lessons, events, and simple food and drink.
idea.customer: Golfers, families, beginners, and groups near a driving range.
idea.offer: A friendlier, upgraded driving range with quality balls and mats, lighting, shelter, practice amenities, and optional programming.
idea.revenue_model: Pay-per-bucket visits, monthly or annual memberships, lessons and events, and a modest food and beverage offering.

key_quotes.quote: We put the time and care into upgrading things that we thought were most important to golfers. So ran some customer surveys, got tangible data to say, "All right, where do we start?"
So we took a little bit of a different approach and we said, hey, instead of prepaying for 10 buckets with one card, let's do a monthly membership model. So we have a model called Ranch Pass.
It was could we build the driving range that we want?

claims.claim: The range had gone from three and a half balls hit per year to 12 million today; the guest affirmed the host's figures.
claims.quote: So, you went from three and a half balls hit per year here 2 or 3 years ago to 12 million today. Yes.

claims.claim: The Ranch Pass costs $20 per month.
claims.quote: It's $20 a month that gets you exclusive pricing.

claims.claim: Members pay 40% less per bucket.
claims.quote: It's 40% less. Oh wow.

claims.claim: About 40% of visitors at the facility are members.
claims.quote: I would say 40% are members.

claims.claim: Food is 15% of the business's revenue.
claims.quote: Food is intentionally a very light part of the business. So 15% of the revenue.

claims.claim: The facility stays open until midnight during summer.
claims.quote: I mean during the summer here we're up until midnight. Um often times we have to like kick people out cuz they're on the putting green and enjoying themselves midnight during the week which is shocking.

claims.claim: The business has 8,000 members across four locations.
claims.quote: So, we've got 8,000 across four locations, mostly monthlies, annual members as well who want to commit to the full year upfront.

claims.claim: Customer lifetime value is described as north of a couple hundred; the currency is not stated.
claims.quote: So varies per site, I would say north of a couple hundred.

claims.claim: The guest estimates lifetime value to customer acquisition cost at about 10 to 1.
claims.quote: Our LTV to CAC is about 10, right?

claims.claim: The host paraphrases the ratio as about $10 back in the first year for every $1 spent acquiring a customer.
claims.quote: So So for every $1 you spend to acquire a customer, you're getting about $10 back in that first year or take.

claims.claim: The business offers a free first bucket at its locations.
claims.quote: One of the offers that we run at all of our locations is a free first bucket. So, welcoming handshake, come try the place completely free.

claims.claim: People will drive past another range for 40 minutes to visit this facility for its putting green.
claims.quote: People who have driving ranges, people who live closer to another driving range that doesn't have a putting green, they will drive past that 40 minutes to come here cuz we have this.

claims.claim: The guest jokingly described regulars' two-hour visits as a "$150 coffee."
claims.quote: They bought a $150 coffee. They were here for 2 hours.

claims.claim: The guest describes irrigation for the whole outfield as a million-dollar expense.
claims.quote: So, we seated it the to run irrigation lines all the way out through the whole outfield exorbitant expense. It's a million dollars.

claims.claim: The current facility is operating at about 85% capacity.
claims.quote: Here, I would say I would say 85%.

claims.claim: The business aims to reach 100,000 members and 50 sites, one in each US state.
claims.quote: We would love 100,000 members and 50 sites, one in every single state across the US.

claims.claim: The Richardson location expects to use 120,000 new balls each year.
claims.quote: You know, the balls here at Richardson, we're going to do 120,000 brand new balls every single year.

claims.claim: Golf balls cost 50 to 70 cents each.
claims.quote: 50 cents to 70 cents a ball.

claims.claim: The picker collects balls about 10 times a day.
claims.quote: Our picker which picks about 10 times a day.

claims.claim: The host says the range is the country's second busiest and expects over 10 million balls to be hit there that year.
claims.quote: So, the second busiest driving range in the country. Over 10 million balls will be hit here this year.

acquisition_channels.details: The guest says paid digital advertising is a large part of acquisition and mentions Facebook and bright rail ads.
Search is used to capture high-intent queries such as "golf lessons near me."
The business uses ads and content to stay top of mind with existing customers and lists Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube.

ideas.delivery: The operator acquires and upgrades physical ranges, then staff run the facility, maintain the grounds and equipment, and serve customers.
ideas.other_uk_rules: For a UK operation, UK GDPR applies to member records and survey data; DMCC Act subscription rules may apply to monthly memberships; Employment Agencies Regs 2003 are relevant if instructors or staff are supplied through an agency.

idea.name: Remote-control ball-picking for kids
idea.one_liner: Add an activity where children use remote-control cars to collect golf balls, with the guest suggesting families may pay to visit for the experience.
idea.customer: Families with children visiting a driving range.
idea.offer: Children drive remote-control cars to collect their own balls and then hit them for free.
idea.revenue_model: A paid visit or activity is suggested, but pricing and the model are not established.

key_quotes.quote: We thought, hey, what if we had remote control cars that kids could go pick up their own balls and then they hit balls for free.
I'm more likely to pay you to come here and do that than actually hit Balt.

claims.claim: The proposed activity would let children collect balls and hit them for free.
claims.quote: We thought, hey, what if we had remote control cars that kids could go pick up their own balls and then they hit balls for free.

claims.claim: The host says they would be more likely to pay to visit for the activity than to hit balls.
claims.quote: I'm more likely to pay you to come here and do that than actually hit Balt.

ideas.delivery: Staff at a driving range would set up and supervise remote-control cars and the ball-collection area.

prices: free ball hitting for participating children

ideas.other_uk_rules: A UK venue would need to account for premises health and safety and child supervision.

idea.name: Topgolf entertainment venues
idea.one_liner: Run golf entertainment venues where customers book time, play golf games, and buy food and drinks.
idea.customer: Groups, casual players, and people seeking a golf-themed outing.
idea.offer: An energetic, occasion-based golf experience with food and beverage service.
idea.revenue_model: Time-based golf bookings plus food, beverage, and events; exact prices are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: The last five minutes is not the best experience because at the Top Golf model, you're you're locked into a certain time. So, at the end of the hour, you're getting rushed out, you're getting a bill,
It's heavy emphasis on food and bev.

claims.claim: Customers are locked into an hour and may feel rushed at the end, with a bill higher than expected.
claims.quote: at the end of the hour, you're getting rushed out, you're getting a bill, it's typically a little bit more than what you expected.

ideas.delivery: Customers visit a physical venue, book a timed golf experience, and can buy food and drinks or attend events.

idea.name: TopTracer Range shot-tracking software
idea.one_liner: License golf shot-tracking technology and range hardware to driving-range operators, with optional coaching tools for instructors and golfers.
idea.customer: Driving-range operators, golf instructors, and golfers using equipped ranges.
idea.offer: Bay-level shot tracking on screens and in a mobile app, plus coaching features for saving student data and sharing drills.
idea.revenue_model: Upfront installation and infrastructure work, followed by per-bay licensing on a multi-year lease; optional product upsells.

key_quotes.quote: Their product is called Top Tracer Range.
A lot of driving range owners are not going to go do this themselves. We should maybe jump that middleman, go out and buy these ranges and do that ourselves.

claims.claim: A quoted hypothetical range operator imagines paying $200,000 to install 50 units; the guest says this was the original pitch to operators.
claims.quote: Oh, I'm going to pay $200,000 to put in 50 of these just so that people can see their their balls on a screen.

claims.claim: The guest says licensing is priced per bay, but does not know the rate off hand.
claims.quote: So, you commit to I'm doing a certain amount of bays. They've got a licensing rate per bay.

claims.claim: The operator pays under a multi-year lease; the monthly amount is not stated.
claims.quote: they're coming in doing the infrastructure and then you're on a multi-year lease that you're paying month end mark.

acquisition_channels.details: Topgolf's original plan was to sell the technology directly to mom-and-pop driving ranges; the exact sales method is not specified.

ideas.delivery: The provider installs and wires equipment at each range, supports the licensed software, and offers coaching features through screens and a mobile app.

prices: $200,000 upfront for 50 units (described as the old pricing model)
multi-year lease; monthly amount not stated

ideas.other_uk_rules: For UK sales, UK GDPR and PECR govern contact data and marketing; the transcript does not specify an outreach channel or the legal form of target operators.

idea.name: Costco membership and loss-leader model
idea.one_liner: Use membership fees and high-value loss leaders to draw repeat visits and earn through the membership relationship.
idea.customer: Members who shop regularly at a warehouse retailer.
idea.offer: A membership paired with low-priced or high-value products that encourage visits and loyalty.
idea.revenue_model: Membership fees and retail sales; the host says membership is where Costco makes its profit.

key_quotes.quote: Costco doesn't really make money on the stuff they sell. They really make their profit on the membership.
Like I love I love Costco chicken. I love Costco $150 hot dogs.

claims.claim: The host says Costco makes its profit on membership rather than the products it sells.
claims.quote: Costco doesn't really make money on the stuff they sell. They really make their profit on the membership.

claims.claim: The guest refers to Costco hot dogs as costing $150, as transcribed.
claims.quote: Like I love I love Costco chicken. I love Costco $150 hot dogs.

ideas.delivery: A warehouse retailer sells products to members in physical locations.
ideas.other_uk_rules: For a UK membership offer, DMCC Act subscription rules may apply; UK GDPR applies to member data.

idea.name: Starbucks gift-card model
idea.one_liner: Sell prepaid gift cards to coffee customers; the transcript uses Starbucks as an example of balances that can remain on a card for years.
idea.customer: Coffee shop customers buying for themselves or as gifts.
idea.offer: Stored-value gift cards redeemable for coffee shop purchases.
idea.revenue_model: Prepaid value is later redeemed for purchases; other details are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: all right I get a Starbucks gift card money could be on there for like 3 years

claims.claim: The guest says a Starbucks gift-card balance could remain on the card for about three years.
claims.quote: all right I get a Starbucks gift card money could be on there for like 3 years

idea.name: Coffee shop with an RC sandpit
idea.one_liner: Pair a coffee shop with a sandpit where children use remote-control cars to move sand; the transcript does not state the revenue model.
idea.customer: Families with children and adults looking for a café visit.
idea.offer: Coffee shop seating plus a children's remote-control car and sandpit activity.

key_quotes.quote: the coffee shop with uh the sand pit and then kids playing remote control cars to pick up and move sand.
